A patch release over five reported issues: four kinds of report that should never have fired, and
one crash. No new check was added, no rule was enabled, no option changed and no default moved.

For a project that already lints to completion, the upgrade can only lower the report count. The
one exception is #12: a file that used to end the run with a `TypeError` now lints to the end, so
the violations the crash was hiding in the rest of that file are reported for the first time.
They are not new checks and not regressions, but to anyone watching a number they are new
reports. The effect is bounded to files that contain a dynamic import whose source is not a
string literal, and nothing else in this release can make the plugin report more.

## Fixes

### A dynamic import whose source is not a string literal no longer crashes the run (#12)

`import(path)`, ``import(`./locales/${locale}.json`)`` and `import(String(path))` threw a
`TypeError` out of `layers-slices`, `absolute-relative` and `public-api`, which ended the lint of
the file that held them. Such an import carries no path the rules can read, so it is now skipped
and the rest of the file is linted. A dynamic import written with a string literal is unchanged
and is still validated.

Read the paragraph at the top of these notes before comparing report counts across the upgrade.
None of the twelve projects measured for this release loses a file to this crash today, so the
measured exposure is zero, but a project of yours may differ.

### An import that never leaves its slice is no longer reported (#41)

In `layers-slices` and in `public-api`. `widgets/header/Header.ts` importing
`@/widgets/header/hooks` was read as one slice importing another and reported as a cross-slice
import, because `hooks` is not one of the built-in segment names `ui`, `model`, `lib`, `api`,
`config` and `assets`, and the slice is then taken from the last part of the path. Both
directions are covered, so `features/leaderboard/actions/get-top.ts` importing
`@/features/leaderboard/lib/utils` is silent too, in both rules. An import that does leave the
slice is still reported by both.

This does not close #41. The slice boundary is still derived from the path string alone, and a
path alone cannot tell a group folder from a slice folder, so the suppression is deliberately
kept to the case where one side's slice directory contains the other side's path. Where the
current file and its target both sit in folders that are not built-in segments, the import is
still reported. Resolving the slice boundary from the filesystem closes that case and is
scheduled for the next release.

### A file inside a slice's `@x` folder may reach its own slice (#40)

In `public-api` and in `layers-slices`. An `@x` file is the cross-import public api of the slice
that holds it, so reaching that same slice is neither a public api violation nor a cross-slice
import. `entities/user/@x/session.ts` re-exporting from `../model/create-user` was reported by
`public-api`, and the import form of the same statement was reported by `layers-slices` as well.
Relative, aliased and bare specifiers are all covered. An `@x` file reaching another slice's
internals is still reported by both rules, and an `@x` folder placed on the layer rather than
inside a slice stands for no slice and is still reported. It silences one shape beyond the issue:
an `@x` folder placed directly on a group folder, such as `entities/group/@x/bar.ts` reaching
`@/entities/group/other/model/x`, was reported on 2.0.0 and is silent now, because a path alone
cannot say whether `group` is a slice or a group folder.

### A file name is no longer read as a segment (#35)

In `no-cross-segment-reexport`. In `entities/cart/services/cart-service.ts`,
`export * from './helpers'` was reported as a re-export across the segments `cart-service` and
`helpers`, with a suggestion pointing at the barrel of the folder the file sits in. Neither name
is a segment: when no folder of the path is a known segment, the rule fell back to the last
component of the path, which for a file is its file name.

This silences more than the shape in the issue, and the wider effect is stated here rather than
left to be discovered. Where no folder of the path is a known segment, a file standing in segment
position is no longer read as a segment at all, so `entities/cart/store.ts` re-exporting `./api`
is now silent. A segment written as a folder is unaffected, and so is a file whose name is one of
the built-in segment names: `entities/cart/model.ts` re-exporting `./api` still reports, as do
`entities/user/model/index.ts` re-exporting `../api` and `entities/cart/services/index.ts`
re-exporting `../model`. Measured across the eight public FSD projects this release was checked
against, the rule produces one report on 2.0.0, and this change removes it.

The other half of #35, the rule reading the `segments` option instead of the built-in list, is
unchanged.

### `ignoreFiles` and `ignoreImports` match under a directory whose name starts with a dot (#34)

picomatch's `**` does not cross a path segment that begins with a dot, so a checkout under
`.worktrees/`, `.cache/` or any other dotted directory stopped matching a pattern such as
`**/entities/**` and the file was linted after all. The same held for an import path carrying a
dotted segment, such as `src/.generated/entities/api`.

The dot-aware match is applied as a widening of the plain one and never in its place, so a
pattern that ignores a file on 2.0.0 still ignores it on 2.0.1. This matters for negated
patterns, which a dot-aware matcher on its own would invert: with `ignoreFiles: ['!src/**']`,
`src/.env.ts` is ignored on both versions, where a plain switch to a dot-aware matcher would have
started reporting it.

The other half of #34, the layer public api check of `public-api` under a dot path, is unchanged.

## Still open

* `#41`: an import that stays inside one slice is still reported when the current file and its
  target both sit in folders that are not built-in segments.
* `#35` and `#37`: `no-cross-segment-reexport` and `absolute-relative` do not read the `segments`
  option yet.
* `#34`: the layer public api check of `public-api` does not fire under a directory whose name
  starts with a dot.
* `#38`: `layers-slices` misses a default import combined with inline type specifiers only.
* `#27`: `layers-slices` visits imports only, so `export ... from` bypasses the layer and slice
  checks that the equivalent import goes through.
